metadata.description: Mapping the Biblical narrative onto the Cornish landscape.

amphitheatres.name: St Just Plen-an-Gwari
amphitheatres.note: The primary heart of Cornish drama.

amphitheatres.name: Piran Round
amphitheatres.note: A massive stage for the spectacle of the Resurrection.

stage_stations.name: Heaven (Celum)
stage_stations.description: The high station for God and the Angels.
stage_stations.visual: A gilded scaffold with a winch system.

stage_stations.name: Hell (Infernum)
stage_stations.description: The 'Hell-Mouth' where Lucifer and the devils dwell.
stage_stations.visual: A gaping dragon's jaw with red lighting and smoke.

stage_stations.name: Solomon's Temple
stage_stations.description: Where the holy wood is tested and Maximilla is martyred.

cornish_land_grants.name: Carnsew
cornish_land_grants.context: Given to the carpenters by Solomon in Act III.
cornish_land_grants.significance: A real medieval manor; its mention made the story feel local.

cornish_land_grants.name: Bejowans
cornish_land_grants.context: Reward for the laborers in the play.
cornish_land_grants.significance: Located right next to the theatre; likely caused a cheer from the crowd.

cornish_land_grants.name: Penryn
cornish_land_grants.significance: The intellectual home where the play was written.
